analysis.answer: Current law allows abortion at any point before fetal viability. The proposed measure changes this by prohibiting physicians from performing abortions after 15 weeks of gestation, with narrow exceptions for medical emergencies threatening the life or major bodily functions of the pregnant woman.

Patients seeking an abortion after 15 weeks may travel to other jurisdictions, seek alternative methods, or carry the pregnancy to term. Physicians will have to adapt their practices to the 15-week limit; because the medical emergency exceptions rely on interpreting terms like "serious risk" and "substantial," some providers might delay or deny care in borderline cases to avoid potential legal liability.

The measure addresses the timeline during which abortions can be legally performed, seeking to shift the cutoff earlier in the pregnancy. The mechanism—a direct prohibition on physicians performing the procedure after 15 weeks—achieves this, though it may create challenges for patients needing care after that point and for doctors determining when the medical exceptions apply.

flags.quote: serious risk of substantial and irreversible physical impairment of a major bodily function
flags.note: The clinical threshold for these conditions is not strictly defined in the text, potentially leaving physicians uncertain about when the exception legally applies.
